title: Lesson 1: What Is Everything Made Of? The Mystery of Matter

slides.title: 🔍 Look Around You! Everything is Something

props.content: The Word of the Day: MATTER
In everyday speech, we use words like 'stuff', 'things', or 'objects'. But scientists have one powerful word that covers EVERYTHING in the physical world: MATTER.

props.alt: Examples of matter: rocks, water bottle, trees, clouds, puppies
props.caption: From giant planets down to microscopic dust — it's ALL matter!

props.text: Matter is anything that has mass and takes up space.
props.author: Scientific Definition

items: 🍎 The apple in your lunchbox = MATTER
🥛 The milk in your glass = MATTER
🎈 The invisible air inside a balloon = MATTER!

props.title: Match the Everyday Object to Why It's Matter

pairs.right: Has lots of mass & takes up space in the room

props.text: The scientific word for all physical stuff in the universe is {{blank}}.

props.content: The Two Golden Rules of Matter
To qualify as matter, an item MUST pass two tests. If it passes both, it's matter! If it fails even one, it is NOT matter.

data: The amount of 'stuff' inside it (gives it weight)

props.content: Rule 1: What is MASS?
Mass is how much material is squeezed inside an object. An elephant has a HUGE mass. A tiny feather has a SMALL mass. But BOTH have mass!
Rule 2: What is VOLUME?
Volume is the amount of space an object occupies. If you step into a full bathtub, the water level rises because YOUR body takes up volume and pushes water out of the way!

cards.back: How much matter/stuff is inside an object (measured in grams or kg).
How much 3D space an object takes up (measured in litres or cm³).
YES! If you weigh a blown-up balloon, it is heavier than an empty balloon!

questions.question: What two conditions MUST be met for something to be called matter?

options.text: It must be hard and cold
It must have mass and take up volume (space)
It must be visible to the human eye

questions.explanation: Matter MUST have mass (weight/stuff) AND volume (take up space).

slides.title: 🕵️ Detective Challenge: Matter vs NOT Matter

props.content: The Trick Questions: What ISN'T Matter?

Here is where even adult scientists get tripped up! Not everything you can see, hear, or feel is matter. Things like light, sound, heat, and feelings are forms of ENERGY or concepts — they do NOT have mass and do NOT take up physical space!

props.title: Interactive Scene: Click items to investigate if they are Matter!

hotspots.label: Sunlight ☀️
hotspots.content: NOT MATTER! Light is energy. It has no mass and doesn't take up physical space.

hotspots.label: Wooden Desk 🪵
hotspots.content: MATTER! Wood has mass and takes up volume in the room.

hotspots.label: Shadow on Wall 👥
hotspots.content: NOT MATTER! A shadow is just the absence of light. You can't weigh a shadow!

hotspots.label: Water Bottle 💧
hotspots.content: MATTER! Liquid water has mass and takes up volume.

props.title: Sort items into Matter or NOT Matter!

questions.question: Is a shadow considered matter?

options.text: Yes, because you can see it
No, because a shadow has no mass and takes up no physical space

questions.explanation: Correct! Seeing something does not automatically make it matter. A shadow has 0 grams of mass!

questions.question: What about heat coming from a radiator?

options.text: It is energy, NOT matter
It is matter because it warms your hands

questions.explanation: Heat is thermal energy, not physical matter!

slides.title: 🧊 The Three Secret Disguises of Matter

props.content: Meet the 3 States of Matter
Think of matter like a master of disguise. Depending on conditions, matter appears in THREE primary physical forms called States of Matter.

props.alt: Ice cube (Solid), Glass of water (Liquid), Steam from kettle (Gas)
props.caption: Water in its three famous states: Solid ice, Liquid water, and Gas steam!

items: 🧊 SOLID: Rigid, keeps its own shape, hard to squash (e.g. rocks, wood, ice).
💧 LIQUID: Flows, changes shape to fit its container, fixed volume (e.g. water, milk, oil).
💨 GAS: Fills all available space, no fixed shape, can be compressed (e.g. air, steam, helium).

cards.back: Has a fixed shape and fixed volume. Example: Brick, Diamond.
Has a fixed volume but takes the shape of its container. Example: Juice, Rain.
Has NO fixed shape and NO fixed volume. Expands everywhere! Example: Oxygen.

pairs.right: Takes the shape of whatever cup it is poured into
Spreads out to fill the ENTIRE room or container

props.content: Why Do States Behave Differently?
If you had super-powered atomic goggles, you'd discover that ALL matter is built from microscopic building blocks called PARTICLES.

data: Slide and roll past each other
Far apart with lots of empty space
Zoom around fast in all directions

questions.question: How do particles move in a solid?

options.text: They fly around at high speed
They vibrate in place while held tightly together
They roll and slide past each other

questions.explanation: Solid particles are locked in position, vibrating like trembling dancers!

questions.question: Why can gas be squashed (compressed)?

options.text: Because gas particles are soft
Because there is lots of empty space between gas particles

questions.explanation: Yes! The empty space allows particles to be pushed closer together when compressed.

props.content: Case Study: The Magic of Water (H₂O)
Did you know that water is one of the ONLY substances on Earth that naturally exists as a solid, a liquid, AND a gas in daily life?

items: 🥶 Freeze water below 0°C → It turns into SOLID Ice!
🛋️ Keep water at room temperature → It remains LIQUID Water!
🔥 Heat water above 100°C → It turns into GAS Steam / Water Vapour!

props.alt: Ice cube melting into water glass and steam rising from kettle
props.caption: Same chemical particles — completely different behavior based on temperature!

props.title: Water State Change Lab
props.text: When solid ice melts, it becomes liquid {{blank}}. When liquid water boils, it becomes gaseous {{blank}}.

Test your detective skills by matching each item with its correct state of matter category!

props.title: Match Item to State of Matter

cards.front: Is Sand a Solid or Liquid?
cards.back: SOLID! Even though sand pours, each grain of sand has its own fixed shape!

cards.front: Is Jelly a Solid or Liquid?
cards.back: Jelly is a mixture called a colloid (liquid trapped inside solid mesh)!

props.content: Final Assessment: Detective Certification 🏆
Answer all 5 questions correctly to earn your Junior Science Detective badge!

questions.question: 1. What is the definition of matter?

options.text: Anything that is shiny and heavy
Anything that has mass and takes up space
Anything that flows like water

questions.explanation: Matter MUST have mass and volume!

questions.question: 2. Which of the following is NOT matter?

options.text: Air inside a ball
Sunlight
Ice cube

questions.explanation: Sunlight is energy, not physical matter!

questions.question: 3. Which state of matter keeps its own shape and volume?

options.text: Solid
Liquid
Gas

questions.explanation: Solids maintain fixed shape and volume.

questions.question: 4. What happens to particles in a liquid?

options.text: They are locked tight and vibrate in place
They slide and roll past each other
They shoot far apart in space

questions.explanation: Liquid particles roll and slide freely.

questions.question: 5. Why does liquid take the shape of its container?

options.text: Because its particles can slide around
Because it has no mass

questions.explanation: Freedom of particle sliding gives liquids container-conforming ability!

props.content: Badge Unlocked: Matter Master 🎖️

props.title: Lesson 1 Summary: What We Mastered Today
props.content: Congratulations Science Detective! You have cracked the mystery of matter.
keyPoints: Matter is anything that has MASS (weight) and VOLUME (space).
Light, sound, heat, and shadows are NOT matter — they are energy or optical effects.
Three primary states: Solid, Liquid, Gas.
Particle theory explains behavior: Solid (vibrate), Liquid (slide), Gas (fly freely).
